questions.problem: Find the equation of the normal line to the surface $z=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+y)$ at the point $(1,-1,0).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+y) \\ 0 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+y)-z\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, if we set $f(x,y,z)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+y)-z$, then our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=0.$ 

A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point $(1,-1,0)$ can be found by computing $∇f(1,-1,0).$

So, we find the gradient and evaluate it at $(1,-1,0):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+y)-z)i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+y)-z)j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+y)-z)k \\  & =\frac{2}{2x+y}\text{ }i+\frac{1}{2x+y}\text{ }j-1\text{ }k \\ ∇f(1,-1,0) & =\frac{2}{2(1)+(-1)}\text{ }i+\frac{1}{2(1)+(-1)}\text{ }j-k \\  & =2\text{ }i+\,j-k \\  & =⟨2,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by using the symmetric form of the equation of the line that is parallel to the vector $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y},{v}_{z}⟩$ and passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$,  we get: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}} \\ \frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y-(-1)}{1}=\frac{z-0}{-1} \\ \frac{x-1}{2}=y+1=-z\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the plane curve $\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}+{y}^{2}=1.$  Find the equation of the normal line to the curve at the point $(3,0).$
questions.worked_solution:
If we set $f(x,y)=\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}+{y}^{2}$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=1.$  

A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(3,0)$ can be found by computing $∇f(3,0).$ 

So, we find the gradient and evaluate it at $(3,0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}+{y}^{2})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}+{y}^{2})\,j \\  & =\frac{2}{9}x\,i+2y\,j \\ ∇f(3,0) & =\frac{2}{9}(3)\,i+2(0)\,j \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\,i \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{3},0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $∇f(3,0)=⟨\frac{2}{3},0⟩$ is a normal vector to the curve at $(3,0).$

Finally, the Cartesian equation of the line that is parallel to $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y}⟩$ and passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-{x}_{0}){v}_{y}-(y-{y}_{0}){v}_{x} & =0 \\ (x-3)0-(y-0)\frac{2}{3} & =0 \\ -\frac{2}{3}y & =0 \\ y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)=x{e}^{y}+y{e}^{z}+z{e}^{x},$ find a vector that's perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(0,0,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(0,0,1)$ can be found by computing 
$∇f(0,0,1).$ 

So, we first find the gradient and evaluate it at $(x,y,z)=(0,0,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{e}^{y}+y{e}^{z}+z{e}^{x})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{e}^{y}+y{e}^{z}+z{e}^{x})\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x{e}^{y}+y{e}^{z}+z{e}^{x})\,k \\  & =({e}^{y}+z{e}^{x})\,i+(x{e}^{y}+{e}^{z})\,j+(y{e}^{z}+{e}^{x})\,k \\ ∇f(0,0,1) & =({e}^{0}+(1){e}^{0})i+((0){e}^{0}+{e}^{1})j+((0){e}^{1}+{e}^{0})k \\  & =2\,i+e\,j+k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $2\,i+e\,j+k$ is perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(0,0,1).$

questions.problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)=2{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-{z}^{2},$ find a vector that's perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,0,-2).$
questions.worked_solution:
A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,0,-2)$ can be found by computing 
$∇f(1,0,-2).$  

So, we first find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$  and evaluate it at $(x,y,z)=(1,0,-2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-{z}^{2})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-{z}^{2})\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(2{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-{z}^{2})\,k \\  & =4x\text{ }i+4y\text{ }j-2z\text{ }k \\ ∇f(1,0,-2) & =4(1)\,i+4(0)\,j-2(-2)\,k \\  & =4\,i+4\,k\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $4\,i+4\,k$ is perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,0,-2).$

questions.problem: Find the equation of the normal line to the surface ${e}^{x+y+z}-2xyz=-3$ at the point $(2,-1,-1).$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's set $f(x,y,z)={e}^{x+y+z}-2xyz.$ Then, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=-3.$ 

A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point $(2,-1,-1)$ can be found by computing $∇f(2,-1,-1).$ 

So, we find the gradient and evaluate it at $(2,-1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{x+y+z}-2xyz)i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{x+y+z}-2xyz)j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({e}^{x+y+z}-2xyz)k \\  & =({e}^{x+y+z}-2yz)\text{ }i+({e}^{x+y+z}-2xz)\text{ }j+({e}^{x+y+z}-2xy)\text{ }k \\ ∇f(2,-1,-1) & =({e}^{2-1-1}-2(-1)(-1))\text{ }i+({e}^{2-1-1}-2(2)(-1))\text{ }j+({e}^{2-1-1}-2(2)(-1))\text{ }k \\  & =({e}^{0}-2)\text{ }i+({e}^{0}+4)\text{ }j+({e}^{0}+4)\text{ }k \\  & =-i+5\,j+5\,k \\  & =⟨-1,5,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the Cartesian equation of the line that is parallel to $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y},{v}_{z}⟩$ and passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}} \\ \frac{x-2}{(-1)}=\frac{y-(-1)}{5}=\frac{z-(-1)}{5} \\ \frac{x-2}{(-1)}=\frac{y+1}{5}=\frac{z+1}{5} \\ 2-x=\frac{y+1}{5}=\frac{z+1}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
